scene.note: The handbook is cut into small pieces of whole words, and every piece remembers which article it came from and where.

args:
Bring the kayak back to the slipway by the time on your ticket.
Rinse the spray deck under the tap, then hand the paddles in at the hut window.

entries.value: the returns note, over two lines

steps.note: The returns note goes in with a size of 45 characters, line break and all.
Spaces, tabs and line breaks all separate words, and a chunk joins its words with single spaces.
Each chunk takes as many words as fit in size, then the next chunk begins. No word is ever cut in two.
A word longer than size still goes in whole, as a chunk of its own. Blank text gives no chunks at all.

entries.value: strings of whole words, in order

steps.note: Back comes a list of strings that, read in order, hold every word of the note once.

args: The tide turns twice a day at the harbour mouth. Ask at the hut for the times before you set out, and stay inside the yellow buoys when it runs fast.

steps.note: The tides note goes in with a size of 60 and an overlap of 15 characters.
First the settings are checked: a size below 1, a negative overlap, or an overlap not smaller than size is an Error.
The first chunk fills up to size, the same way as before.
The next chunk opens with the last words of the one before, as many as fit in overlap, then fills up to size again.
No chunk carries the whole chunk before it, so each one starts at least a word further on. The last chunk ends with the note's last word.

entries.value: strings whose edges repeat a few words

steps.note: Back comes a list of strings, where a fact on the edge of one chunk also sits in the next.

args.title: Using the slipway
args.text: Wait for the boat ahead to clear the slipway. Carry the kayak with a partner and never drag it over the stones.

args.title: The kit room
args.text: Spray decks hang on the left wall and helmets sit on the shelf by the door.

steps.note: Two new articles go in, each with an id, a title and a text, plus a size of 50 and an overlap of 10.
Each article's text is cut with chunkText and the same size and overlap.
Every chunk string becomes a Chunk. index counts from 0 again in each article, so the id is unique across the handbook.
All chunks come back in one flat list, in article order. An article with empty text adds none.
The demo prints how many chunks each article gave, so you can see the whole handbook cut up.
